problemSets.title: 8.01 Classical Mechanics Pset 1
problemSets.text: 1. Car and Bicycle Rider. A car is driving along a straight line with a speed v0. At time t = 0 the car is at the origin. At a later instant of time t = t1 the car starts to slow down until it stops at a time t = t2. The acceleration of the car is a_c = 0 for 0 < t < t1 and a_c = -c(t - t1) for t1 < t < t2, where c is a positive constant with dimensions of acceleration per unit time. (a) Find v_c(t) and x_c(t) in terms of v0, c, t, t1 and t2. (b) A bicycle rider rides at a constant speed v_b and at t = 0 is 17 m behind the car. The cyclist reaches the car when the car just comes to rest. Use v0 = 12 m/s, t1 = 1 s and c = 6 m/s^3. Find the speed of the bicycle to 2 significant figures.

references.label: Shamith Kandregula, MIT8_01F16 pset 1 solutions (handwritten, student-made, unofficial)
references.answers:
Unofficial handwritten solutions by a high-school student; the author warns of possible calculation mistakes.

P1: v_c = v0 for t<t1 and v_c = v0 - (c/2)(t-t1)^2 for t1<t<t2. x_c = v0 t for t<t1 and x_c = v0 t - (c/6)(t-t1)^3 for t1<t<t2. Part b (numbers used: v0=18, c=3, t1=1; the 18 is hard to read in the scan): car stops when v=0, so (t-1)^2=4, t-1=2, t2=3 s. Stopping position x_c = 36 - (1/2)(2)^3 = 28 m. The bicycle covers 45 m in 3 s, so v_b = 15 m/s.

Here is Problem Set 1, Problem 1 of 5 (MIT OpenCourseWare, 8.01SC Classical Mechanics, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

**Car and Bicycle Rider.** A car drives along a straight line at speed v0 and is at the origin at t = 0. It keeps constant velocity until t = t1, then slows with a(t) = -c(t - t1) until it stops at t = t2.

**(a)** Find v(t) and x(t) for the car in terms of v0, c, t, t1 and t2.

**(b)** A cyclist riding at constant speed v_b starts 17 m behind the car at t = 0 and reaches the car exactly when the car comes to rest. Use v0 = 12 m/s, t1 = 1 s and c = 6 m/s^3. Find v_b to 2 significant figures.

Work (a) first, since integrating a(t) twice gives v and x in each phase. Enter v_b below.

problemSets.title: 8.01 Classical Mechanics Pset 1
problemSets.text: 1. Car and Bicycle Rider. A car is driving along a straight line with a speed v0. At time t = 0 the car is at the origin. At a later instant of time t = t1 the car starts to slow down until it stops at a time t = t2. The acceleration of the car is a_c = 0 for 0 < t < t1 and a_c = -c(t - t1) for t1 < t < t2, where c is a positive constant with dimensions of acceleration per unit time. (a) Find v_c(t) and x_c(t) in terms of v0, c, t, t1 and t2. (b) A bicycle rider rides at a constant speed v_b and at t = 0 is 17 m behind the car. The cyclist reaches the car when the car just comes to rest. Use v0 = 12 m/s, t1 = 1 s and c = 6 m/s^3. Find the speed of the bicycle to 2 significant figures.

references.label: Shamith Kandregula, MIT8_01F16 pset 1 solutions (handwritten, student-made, unofficial)
references.answers:
Unofficial handwritten solutions by a high-school student; the author warns of possible calculation mistakes.

P1: v_c = v0 - (c/2)(t-t1)^2 for t1<t<t2; x_c = v0 t - (c/6)(t-t1)^3. Part b: t2 = 3 s, stopping position 28 m, so v_b = 28/3 = 9.3 m/s.
